items.title: Make the first-fight control legend readable
items.what: On the main fight screen, the bottom-center brown legend above the sticks packs both STANCE and TECHNIQUE instructions into a short strip with very small arrow glyphs and text like “◄ step ▲ jump / ► step ▼ crouch”; the duplicated “step” labels require close reading.
items.why: This is the player’s first explanation of the twin-stick controls. On a phone, with thumbs already covering the lower third, the mapping is too slow to parse before the 30-second round starts.
items.how: Replace the strip with two larger per-stick diagrams during onboarding: 16–18 CSS px labels, left/right labeled “step left/right,” up “jump,” down “crouch,” and the right stick labeled “back/forward/up/down.” Highlight one direction at a time during countdown, then collapse after the first round.

items.title: Make loading progress unmistakable
items.what: On the ShoeMoney pre-boot loading screen, the progress bar in the lower third is only a thin brown line with a faint center glint; there is no clear filled portion, percent, or changing phase text.
items.why: A mobile WebGPU load can pause on assets or shader compilation. With this bar, the first screen can look stalled even while the game is working.
items.how: Use a 10–12px-high track with a distinct warm-gold left-to-right fill, add a numeric percent, and rotate concrete status text such as “Loading fighters,” “Compiling shaders,” and “Preparing dojo.” Keep the palette warm; just make state visible.

items.title: Stop making countdowns look like inactive buttons
items.what: On the pre-fight and results screens, the large gold rounded rectangle reads “FIGHT IN 2” or “REMATCH IN 8,” but it is styled exactly like the primary tap button while the sticks below are dimmed.
items.why: Touch players will naturally tap the biggest button-shaped object and may think the game ignored them if it is only a timer.
items.how: If it is not tappable, restyle it as a non-button countdown badge reading “Starts in 2.” If it is tappable, change the copy to “Tap to fight” / “Rematch now” and show the countdown as smaller secondary text.

items.title: Turn the Techniques screen into a scannable phone reference
items.what: The Techniques modal shows many rows at once, each with two tiny circular arrow icons, a plus sign, a move name, and small right-aligned point text; the “RIGHT STICK DOWN” section begins at the bottom edge with no visible scroll affordance.
items.why: During a 30-second bout, this is too dense to use as a quick reference. Players need to recognize a move pattern at a glance, not decode a wall of symbols.
items.how: Split the list into Forward/Back/Up/Down tabs or accordions, enlarge the combo icons and point tags, pin a “starter moves” card at the top, and add a visible scroll bar or bottom fade so players know more content continues.

items.title: Lock or redesign the landscape layout
items.what: In the landscape screenshot, the arena occupies only the upper band, the lower portion becomes a large empty black control area, the sticks sit far out in the corners, and the HUD text is tiny across the top.
items.why: If a mobile browser opens while rotated, the game looks unfinished and the controls are harder to reach, even though the portrait layout is the intended experience.
items.how: Either force portrait with a full-screen “Rotate your phone” overlay, or build a real landscape layout: enlarge the fighters and HUD, center the arena vertically, and place larger sticks closer to natural thumb positions.
